read_only.applicability: HTTP console methods classified as mutating, including multipart send/upload. This is not the structural mob-events stale-cursor meaning of -32010; discriminate by method and data.

access_denied.applicability: Applicable ABAC action gates and access-administration checks. Additional denial context may be present. Some reads filter results instead of refusing the whole request; this is not an unconditional error on every method.

candidate_launch.applicability: A runtime-backed console of a candidate launch (runtime_options.mob_composition.authority = candidate) refuses, before anything is read or written, the methods that retire, respawn or reset a member, recompute the roster or rewire members (meta/retire, meta/retire_member, meta/respawn, meta/respawn_member, meta/reset, meta/reset_all, meta/delete_identity, meta/reconcile_identity and meta/topology/apply; meta/reconcile_edges answers a dry run flagged applied: false instead), meta/gating/decide, the console schedule writes (meta/schedule/create, update, pause, resume and delete), the ones that create a session (meta/ensure_member, meta/spawn_helper, meta/fork_helper, meta/fork_member and meta/attach_existing_session), the ones that admit member input or act on a member's runs (among them meta/console/send, including multipart, meta/console/voice/open, meta/console/recover_send, meta/run_flow, meta/reload_member, meta/stop_member_run and meta/force_cancel_member), the member declaration mutations (mob/adopt_member_identity_declaration and mob/apply_member_tool_declaration), and the operator mutations: the WorkGraph writes, meta/memory/quarantine/decide, the agent memory writes, the label sets and deletes, the access policy writes, meta/console/revoke_sessions, meta/console/attention/dismiss, meta/blob/upload, meta/cancel_flow, the live channel verbs, a mobpack deploy with execute or a validation with rkat_validate, and a draft write (meta/mobpacks/create, save, delete, undo and redo) except to a store file the caller names outside the state directory and the gateway home that is not the store META_FLOW_EDITOR_DRAFT_STORE names. Reads still answer.

approver_unauthenticated.applicability: Console approval decisions (meta/gating/decide, meta/memory/quarantine/decide and meta/workgraph/goal/confirm): the caller is not a verified, current person (no token on an open console, a service token, a token that names no human, a shared-account token), or the person's login ended (its token expired or its sessions were revoked) while the decision waited. A login that ended before the console took the request up is -32056 caller_not_current instead. Nothing was decided.

person_authentication_required.applicability: A console WorkGraph claim or release (meta/workgraph/claim, meta/workgraph/release) made on an open console without a token: a claim is owned by its caller, and such a caller owns nothing. Nothing was changed.

errors.note: -32602 with data.kind side_chat_restart_refused (operation respawn, agent_identity, source_member_id) refuses a console side chat, which is never respawned: its successor would be no fork of its source. Close it and fork the source again. meta/respawn_member, outside this contract, refuses it the same way.

-32602 with data.kind side_chat_restart_refused (operation reset, agent_identity, source_member_id) refuses a console side chat, which is never reset: its successor would be no fork of its source. Close it and fork the source again.

request.note: run_id is the member run's UUID from its run_started event (identity.run_id). A stale run_id is the typed not_current receipt, never an interrupt.

success.note: receipt is meerkat's WireRunStopReceipt, tagged by outcome: stopped { run_id, contributors }, not_current { run_id, current_run_id? } or not_stoppable { run_id, state }.

errors.note: Mob refusals (unknown member, unsupported member mode, host refusal) carry meerkat's typed code and structured data.

request.note: A side chat: a durable fork of the source's committed transcript end into a new member named agent_identity, with the source's role, profile and model overrides, runtime mode and tools, seated exempt from the mob definition's wiring rules so it is never wired to a peer whatever the source's role, and kept until it is retired, which needs agent.retire on the source. Gated on agent.spawn for agent_identity and on agent.view and agent.send for the source (-32030 naming the refused action); a source whose lineage already fills the access rules' walk (the source and seven ancestors) is refused -32030 with data.reason lineage_too_deep, for every caller, an admin included. A source the console's visibility policy hides is answered as unknown (-32001, data.kind identity_hidden_by_policy), as meta/fork_helper, outside this contract, answers it. A message_count (prefix) is refused. Offered in meta/capabilities where sessions persist, or where the composition did not record whether they do (the fork then refuses typed where they do not).

success.note: retention is until_closed. instructions lists each instruction the side chat inherited as history: state inherited (the source's revision activated in the side chat) or inactive with a reason (not_effective_in_source, body_unreadable, activation_refused); the side chat refuses its first turn naming an inactive key. The experience lists a side chat's sidebar row with side_chat_of, its source's identity; its console labels carry side_chat_of and side_chat_of_session (the forked source session), read from the durable fork record, and every agent check on a side chat is its source's: an allow must match the source or its lineage, and a rule that matches only the side chat grants nothing. A side chat is never respawned or reset (meta/respawn and meta/reset answer -32602 side_chat_restart_refused) and never adopted as an identity (mob/adopt_member_identity_declaration answers -32602 side_chat_adoption_refused).

errors.note: -32055 is a typed refusal: data.kind fork_source_unavailable (cause running, no_session for a seat that was never woken, which the fork does not wake, remote_read_unavailable or authority_unavailable), nothing forked; fork_source_changed (agent_identity, source_member_id), a side chat forked from another session of the source than the fork's checks read (a reset or a respawn ran in between); or unwired_seat_unavailable (wiring.rule seated_with_peers), a seated side chat with peer edges after all. For the last two the side chat is retired again and data.retired says whether that succeeded. -32001 is a source the console's visibility policy hides (identity_hidden_by_policy). Under a member auth binding a source whose session records another binding or none answers -32602 member_auth_binding_uncarried, nothing forked. -32037 is meerkat's fork_instruction_refused under the refuse policy. A committed fork whose seat failed keeps meerkat's fork_member_provision_failed data with its fork_session_id.

request.note: identity names the agent as meta/console/send names it (a public alias; a runtime member id the console knows is read as its identity). Gated on agent.view for the agent (-32030). Offered in meta/capabilities where the runtime's schedule host keeps console schedules; elsewhere the method answers -32601. Console-only: the stdin gateway does not dispatch the meta/schedule/* methods.

success.note: schedules lists the agent's console schedules, oldest first, each a console_schedule: schedule_id, identity, name (or null), content, trigger (the scheduler's trigger, tagged by type: once, interval or calendar), phase (active or paused), revision, sender (the principal the schedule sends as, null for an anonymous caller and when withheld), sender_hidden (true when the caller may view the agent but not send to it: only a caller who may send to the agent sees who its schedules send as), defined_at_utc, created_at_utc, updated_at_utc and next_due_at_utc (the next planned send of an active schedule, else null). The agent's own schedules (its schedule tools) and other schedules of the store are not listed, and the agent's schedule tools neither list nor change console schedules.

errors.note: -32601 where the gateway keeps no console schedules; -32602 for a missing or invalid identity; -32004 data.kind schedule_host_unavailable when the schedule store is unavailable; -32000 (data.error internal_error) when the console cannot read its agents or the store.

request.note: A deferred send of content (a non-empty string) to the agent identity names, at the trigger's times: the scheduler's trigger, tagged by type (once {due_at_utc}, interval {start_at_utc, every_seconds, end_at_utc?} or calendar {timezone, minute, hour, day_of_month, month, day_of_week, year?}, each calendar field {kind: any} or {kind: values, values}); an interval repeats at most once a minute (every_seconds of at least 60). Gated as meta/console/send is on this route, for the caller as the console resolves it, signed in or not: a writable console (-32010), a valid public alias, and agent.send and schedule.manage for the agent under the live access policy (-32030; a configuration that names no schedule action grants schedule.manage wherever it grants agent.send). The schedule records that caller as its sender: the principal the console send would use, with the provider and issuer its token verified under (none for an anonymous caller), and the subject only for a verified signed-in human.

success.note: The schedule as meta/schedule/list answers it. Each due time is sent as a console send by the recorded sender, judged when it fires. The Console first admits the sender as it admits a live request by it: an anonymous sender only while the Console requires no sign-in; a principal only under the issuer the Console trusts then, past its provider policy and allowlist where sign-in is required, and past its session fence (Console sessions revoked after the schedule was defined refuse it, for every signed-in principal, a service identity included). Then it sends exactly as /console/send does once its caller is admitted: the candidate-launch refusal, a writable console, agent.send for the sender under the access policy then, an addressable agent whose input is not governed, and the identity-first send or the member lane. A refused or failed send fails that occurrence (delivery_failed) and the schedule keeps its later times; an agent the console no longer knows (a deleted identity, or a member without one that was retired) fails its sends the same way, and the schedule stays until it is deleted, while an identity released with meta/retire is materialized by the send, as by any console send. A send is deduplicated under its occurrence's delivery key in the sender's send scope, as a live send by the sender is, so a redelivered occurrence is sent once while the console's dedupe store holds the key (an in-memory store forgets it on restart); a send whose admission the Console could not observe (a timeout) is recorded failed although it may have been admitted. Sends carry origin console:schedule and the scheduler turn origin, through the Console router built last (its decisions and visibility); a fire on a gateway with no Console send path waits for one only in the first 30 seconds after the gateway's schedule host starts, and otherwise fails at once.

errors.note: -32001 data.kind unknown_identity when no agent of the console has the name; -32002 data.kind not_addressable for an agent that takes no console sends; -32004 data.kind governed_target for an agent whose input is governed (a governed send needs its Console human present, and a fire has none) or data.kind schedule_host_unavailable where no schedule firing host sends the gateway's schedules; -32602 for an invalid identity, a blank content, an interval under 60 seconds, or an invalid trigger (the scheduler's validation, an unknown time zone among them), and with data.kind unsupported_param (param) for a create that names expected_revision or take_over_sender.

request.note: Changes the console schedule schedule_id of the agent identity names: its content, trigger or name, each kept when absent. Gated as meta/schedule/create. The update defines the schedule again as its caller and judges the agent again as a create does. expected_revision is the schedule's revision as the caller read it: a schedule that moved past it is refused, so a change made from an older read never overwrites one made meanwhile; the update writes at the revision it read either way. A caller who is not the schedule's sender takes it over only with take_over_sender true, and the sender it replaces joins sender_history; the sender's own update keeps the sender and refreshes its definition time.

success.note: The changed schedule. Every update moves the schedule to a new revision and plans its next times again.

errors.note: -32001 data.kind schedule_not_found for a schedule that does not exist, was deleted, is no console schedule, or is another agent's. The other refusals are meta/schedule/create's. -32009 data.kind schedule_revision_conflict (expected_revision, actual_revision) when the schedule moved past the expected_revision the call named, or changed between this call's read and its write: nothing is changed, so the call never overwrites that change. -32009 data.kind sender_takeover_required (sender, who the schedule sends as now) for a caller who is not the schedule's sender and sent no take_over_sender true: nothing is changed. -32602 for an expected_revision that is not a non-negative integer or a take_over_sender that is not a boolean.

request.note: Stops the console schedule's sends until it is resumed; pausing a paused schedule answers it as it is. Gated on a writable console and agent.send and schedule.manage for the agent; the sender stays as it is. It acts on the schedule as it is: it takes no expected_revision and no take_over_sender.

success.note: The schedule as the pause left it.

errors.note: -32001 data.kind schedule_not_found for a schedule that does not exist, was deleted, is no console schedule, or is another agent's; -32602 for an invalid identity or schedule_id, and with data.kind unsupported_param (param) for a pause that names expected_revision or take_over_sender: nothing is changed.

request.note: Resumes a paused console schedule. Gated as meta/schedule/create: the resume defines the schedule again as its caller while it is still paused, at the revision it read, so no send goes out as an earlier sender and no change made meanwhile is put back, and judges the agent again as a create does. expected_revision and take_over_sender work as on meta/schedule/update: a caller who is not the schedule's sender takes it over only with take_over_sender true.

success.note: The schedule as Core resumed it: a change another caller made between the resume's write and the resume shows in the answer (its sender, content and revision).

errors.note: -32001 data.kind schedule_not_found for a schedule that does not exist, was deleted, is no console schedule, or is another agent's. -32602 for a schedule that is not paused. The other refusals are meta/schedule/create's. -32009 data.kind schedule_revision_conflict (expected_revision, actual_revision) when the schedule moved past the expected_revision the call named, or changed between this call's read and its write: nothing is changed, so the call never overwrites that change. -32009 data.kind sender_takeover_required (sender) for a caller who is not the schedule's sender and sent no take_over_sender true: the schedule stays paused and unchanged.

request.note: Deletes the console schedule and its planned sends. Gated on a writable console and agent.send and schedule.manage for the agent. It acts on the schedule as it is: it takes no expected_revision and no take_over_sender.

success.note: deleted is true.

errors.note: -32001 data.kind schedule_not_found for a schedule that does not exist, was deleted, is no console schedule, or is another agent's; -32602 data.kind unsupported_param (param) for a delete that names expected_revision or take_over_sender: nothing is changed.

request.note: HTTP returns a bounded snapshot without cursor pagination. SDK/stdin additionally accepts recipient/sink filters and defaults limit to 20.

success.note: retention is durable when the runtime keeps the gating state across a restart, process when it keeps it in memory.

request.note: The rows a caller reads whole are under decisions, the rows it may see only the status of under statuses; a decision the caller may not see is not listed. decisions.view is needed while access control is enforced.
A caller who may see only the decision's status is refused with -32030, data.kind content_not_visible; a decision it may not see reads as decision_not_found.

The HTTP console takes the approver from the connection: a verified, current person decides as its access principal, with the approver ids it holds through the access configuration. A request that carries approver_id is invalid params (-32602). deny is an HTTP compatibility alias for reject. SDK/stdin requires approver_id and accepts only approve/reject/escalate, and its decisions record deciding_assurance device_trusted.

success.note: The caller's own attention items, newest first, at most 100 from the newest 200 not dismissed: replies meant for the caller alone that no private thread of theirs took. Every console that keeps an attention list serves a verified person the items addressed to them, whatever its posture; every other caller reads an empty list. An item has id, created_at_ms and kind; a private_reply item adds origin {identity, interaction_id, input_frame_id}, the text the payload policies leave of the reply (the host's before the item is stored, this console's as it is read, as they leave the reply's frame in a thread; absent when they leave none) and redacted: true when a policy rewrote it. An item is listed only while the caller may view the agent the request went to. A client shows the kinds it knows and skips the rest. retention is durable or process.
dismissed is false when the caller holds no such item, another person's included. A dismissed item is no longer listed.

expected_content_hash is the record.content_hash returned by meta/memory/panel/record. The reviewer recorded in audit is the signed-in person on the connection; no reviewer field is accepted. Right before the review is applied the console checks the person and reads the caller's grants again: a grant withdrawn while the review waited is -32030.

success.note: decision.review records the verdict, reviewer, bound hash, quarantine reason and rationale, plus expired_promotions (gated promotions past their expiry) and invalidated_promotions (live gated promotions an operator tombstone invalidated in the same transaction).

errors.note: -32043 is a typed refusal (data.kind memory_quarantine_review_refused, data.reason not_found | content_mismatch | not_quarantined | gate_pending | successor_conflict | secret_detected | stale_update); nothing was written. gate_pending refuses a release while a live gated promotion owns the record; an operator tombstone invalidates the promotion instead.

request.note: The claim's owner releases it, and so does an access admin: an admin's release of someone else's claim is a break-glass release, and the work graph's Released event records the admin and the released claim under break_glass. Anyone else is -32030 access_denied. The release is bound to expected_revision, and the caller's grants are read again after the item read.

Only a signed-in person confirms, as itself. After the evidence read, right before the confirmation is applied, the console checks the person and reads the caller's grants again: a grant withdrawn while the confirmation waited is -32030.

Read only. Structural mob events (member_spawned, members_wired, members_unwired and the rest) in cursor order; -32010 here is a stale after_seq cursor (data.error event_query_stale), not the read-only refusal.

Creates the agents (1 to 256, all or nothing), each {name, profile, display_name?, instructions? (an array of sections), context?, labels?, first_message?, peers?, addressability?, runtime_mode_override?}. addressability is addressable (the default) or internal_only; runtime_mode_override is autonomous_host or turn_driven (absent, the agent runs as its profile says). The requester is the signed-in person, or the host on its console surface. Gated on a writable console and agent.identity.create. An unknown member is refused.

success.note: The change's typed outcome, tagged by outcome: done {operation_id, agents: [{name, state, spec_digest?, spec_revision?, session_id?, seat?, instructions?}]}, pending_decision {operation_id, decision_id, deadline_ms} (nothing is written but the decision) or pending_preparation {operation_id, agents}. The same caller, request_id and request answer the same state again and write nothing.

errors.note: -32058 is the family's one refusal: message is the refusal's sentence, and data carries kind (a closed vocabulary), field (a path into the request, when the refusal concerns one field), retryable, detail, and the kind's own members. Params that are not what the method takes are that error too, kind invalid_request. The reads are served on every launch that has agents of its own, with or without an identity policy; a change, and a plan, on a launch without an enabled identity policy is refused kind change_denied. -32601 only on a launch without agents of its own, or once its mob stopped.

request.note: Updates one agent at the spec digest the caller read (a moved spec answers stale_spec with the current one). set {display_name?, instructions?, context?, labels?, labels_remove?, profile?, addressability?, runtime_mode_override?}: an absent member is unchanged. addressability and runtime_mode_override take the values they take on a create; an update sets a runtime mode and cannot return the agent to its profile's. An agent's entry of the outcome says what became of an instructions change. Gated on a writable console and agent.identity.manage for the agent. An unknown member is refused. An agent the caller may not view is answered as a name no agent holds (-32058, kind identity_unknown at name), and nothing is changed.

request.note: Archives one agent: it stops and keeps its name, record, conversation and memory, and its last conversation is harvested as for any agent that leaves. Gated on a writable console and agent.identity.manage for the agent. An unknown member is refused.
